# Interactions

Start interactions, wait for their answers, and take part in a run that is going.

**Library:** [Maitento](index.md#maitento), for apps. More in [Interactions](../../../concepts/interactions.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`InteractionAddMessage`](#interactionaddmessage) | Posts a message from a person into an interaction run that is still going. |
| [`InteractionAwait`](#interactionawait) | Waits until an interaction run has ended (`Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`), then returns the run. |
| [`InteractionAwaitAll`](#interactionawaitall) | Waits until every interaction run in a list has ended, then returns them all. |
| [`InteractionAwaitAny`](#interactionawaitany) | Waits until at least one interaction run in a list has ended, then returns every run in the list that has ended by then. |
| [`InteractionGet`](#interactionget) | Returns an interaction's definition, with every version. |
| [`InteractionGetToolResult`](#interactiongettoolresult) | Returns the stored result of one tool call in an interaction run. |
| [`InteractionList`](#interactionlist) | Returns the interactions in a namespace. |
| [`InteractionProcessGet`](#interactionprocessget) | Returns an interaction run as it is now, without waiting for it. |
| [`InteractionStart`](#interactionstart) | Starts an interaction run and returns its id straight away, without waiting for its answer. |
| [`InteractionStartWithLoomGifts`](#interactionstartwithloomgifts) | Starts an interaction run, as [`InteractionStart`](#interactionstart) does, handing some of its agents threads of memory as they start; returns the run's id straight away. |
| [`InteractionStartWithSwarmLimits`](#interactionstartwithswarmlimits) | Starts an interaction run, as [`InteractionStartWithLoomGifts`](#interactionstartwithloomgifts) does, narrowing how far its sub-interactions may spread; returns the run's id straight away. |
| [`InteractionVoteNo`](#interactionvoteno) | Votes no, as a person, on the vote or proposed solution an interaction run is waiting on, giving a reason. |
| [`InteractionVoteYes`](#interactionvoteyes) | Votes yes, as a person, on the vote or proposed solution an interaction run is waiting on. |

### InteractionAddMessage

Posts a message from a person into an interaction run that is still going.

```c
void InteractionAddMessage(string processId, string message, string authorName, string authorId)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `string` | The interaction run's id. |
| `message` | `string` | The message. It can't be blank. |
| `authorName` | `string`, can be empty | The name the message is shown as coming from. There is no default: `""` records no name. |
| `authorId` | `string`, can be empty | The id of the user to record as its author. Pass `""` for the user this app runs as. |

A run waiting for a person carries on at once. A run that is working gets the message at its next turn. A run that ended because nobody replied in time is woken up again.

Fails with `Interaction process is complete and can no longer accept messages` when the run has ended, `Solution is not ready for message` when it is waiting for a vote (use [`InteractionVoteYes`](#interactionvoteyes) or [`InteractionVoteNo`](#interactionvoteno)), `Invalid process ID format: …`, and `Not found` when your tenant has no interaction run with that id.

### InteractionAwait

Waits until an interaction run has ended (`Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`), then returns the run.

```c
jsonObject InteractionAwait(guid id)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `guid` | The run's id, as [`InteractionStart`](#interactionstart) returned it. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The ended run, as a JSON object.

It checks about twice a second, and has no time limit of its own: it waits as long as the run takes. The interaction's own time limit still applies to the run. A run waiting for a person (to reply, vote or approve a tool call) or for its sub-interactions hasn't ended, so the wait goes on. The wait counts towards this app's own time limit (`duration.max`), and this run records it as `awaitTime`. If this app is stopped while it waits, the wait ends with it.

The run is a JSON object, the same one the API returns for an interaction run. Its most useful fields are `status`; `output`, the answer: text, or JSON text when a response schema applies, and null until there is one; `failureDetails`, why it failed or was stopped; `inputs`, each `{ name, value }`; `context`, the whole conversation; `tokenUsage`; and `id`, `dateStarted`, `dateEnded`, `executionTime`, `parentProcessId` and `rootProcessId`.

Check `status` before you use the result: a run that failed ends the wait too. To read a JSON answer, use [`StringToJsonObject(JsonObjectGet(run, "output"))`](conversion.md#stringtojsonobject). Fails with `Interaction process … not found` when your tenant has no interaction run with that id.

### InteractionAwaitAll

Waits until every interaction run in a list has ended, then returns them all.

```c
jsonArray InteractionAwaitAll(jsonArray ids)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ids` | `jsonArray` | The runs' ids, as a JSON array of the ids [`InteractionStart`](#interactionstart) returned. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of the ended runs.

A run has ended when its `status` is `Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`; check each one's, because a failed run ends the wait too. Each element is the run as [`InteractionAwait`](#interactionawait) returns it. The runs come back in no particular order (not necessarily the order of the ids), so match them up by `id`. An id listed twice comes back once.

It checks about twice a second, and has no time limit of its own. The wait counts towards this app's own time limit (`duration.max`), and this run records it as `awaitTime`. If this app is stopped while it waits, the wait ends with it.

Fails with `At least one process ID is required` for an empty list, `Invalid GUID at index 2: …` for an element that isn't an id, and `Interaction process(es) not found: …` for ids your tenant has no run with.

### InteractionAwaitAny

Waits until at least one interaction run in a list has ended, then returns every run in the list that has ended by then.

```c
jsonArray InteractionAwaitAny(jsonArray ids)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ids` | `jsonArray` | The runs' ids, as a JSON array of the ids [`InteractionStart`](#interactionstart) returned. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of the runs that have ended: at least one.

A run has ended when its `status` is `Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`. Each element is the run as [`InteractionAwait`](#interactionawait) returns it. The runs still going aren't in the result, and keep running: stop the ones you no longer need with [`ProcessKill`](runs.md#processkill).

A run in the list that had already ended makes it return at once, so take the ended runs out of the list before you wait again.

It checks about twice a second, and has no time limit of its own. The wait counts towards this app's own time limit (`duration.max`), and this run records it as `awaitTime`. If this app is stopped while it waits, the wait ends with it.

Fails with `At least one process ID is required` for an empty list, `Invalid GUID at index 2: …` for an element that isn't an id, and `Interaction process(es) not found: …` for ids your tenant has no run with.

### InteractionGet

Returns an interaction's definition, with every version.

```c
jsonObject InteractionGet(string name)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The interaction: `name`, or `name@namespace`. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The interaction, as a JSON object.

Name the interaction as `name`, or `name@namespace` for one in another namespace of your tenant; a name without `@` is looked up in this app's namespace.

The JSON object starts with `$type`, the kind of interaction (`one-shot`, `round-robin` or `managed`), then holds `id`, `name`, `namespaceId`, `dateCreated`, `dateUpdated` and `versions`. Each version has its `version` number, its prompt, agents and inputs (`inputsPrompt` and the like), and its settings, such as `durationAutoTermination`.

Fails with `Not found` when there is no such interaction, and `Namespace '…' was not found.` when the namespace doesn't exist.

### InteractionGetToolResult

Returns the stored result of one tool call in an interaction run.

```c
jsonObject InteractionGetToolResult(string processId, int sequence)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `string` | The interaction run's id. |
| `sequence` | `int` | The `sequence` of the tool result's item in the run's `context`. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The tool result, as a JSON object.

A tool's result can be kept apart from the run, to keep the run small: its item in the run's `context` then has a `toolResultId` and no `result`. This call reads it by that item's `sequence`.

The JSON object holds `result`, the tool's result as kept; `isTruncated`, true when it was too large and was cut short; `originalLength` and `storedLength`, in bytes; `isError`, true when the call failed or a person rejected it; and `toolCallId`, `sequence` and `interactionProcessId`.

Fails with `Invalid process ID format: …`, and `Not found` when your tenant has no such run or it has no stored result at that `sequence`.

### InteractionList

Returns the interactions in a namespace.

```c
jsonArray InteractionList(string namespaceName)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `namespaceName` | `string`, can be empty | The namespace to list. Pass `""` for this app's own namespace. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of interactions.

Each element of the JSON array is an interaction as [`InteractionGet`](#interactionget) returns it. Fails with `Namespace '…' was not found.` when the namespace doesn't exist.

### InteractionProcessGet

Returns an interaction run as it is now, without waiting for it.

```c
jsonObject InteractionProcessGet(string processId)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `string` | The interaction run's id. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The run, as a JSON object.

The run is the JSON object [`InteractionAwait`](#interactionawait) describes. While it is going, its `status` is `New`, `Running`, `HumanInteractionRequired` (waiting for a person to reply or vote), `HumanInteractionComplete`, `PendingApproval` (waiting for a person to approve a tool call) or `AwaitingChildren` (waiting for its sub-interactions); once it has ended, `Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`. Fails with `Invalid process ID format: …` when `processId` isn't an id, and `Not found` when your tenant has no interaction run with that id.

### InteractionStart

Starts an interaction run and returns its id straight away, without waiting for its answer.

```c
string InteractionStart(string name, jsonObject inputs, jsonArray loomMappings, jsonArray aiModelOverrides, string responseJsonSchema)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The interaction to start: `name`, or `name@namespace`. |
| `inputs` | `jsonObject` | The run's inputs, as a JSON object with one key per input, such as `{ "product": "a bamboo cup" }`. Text values are passed as they are; any other JSON value is passed as JSON text. Build it with [`JsonObjectCreate`](json.md#jsonobjectcreate) and [`JsonObjectSetString`](json.md#jsonobjectsetstring). This argument can't be empty: pass `"{}"` when the interaction takes no inputs. |
| `loomMappings` | `jsonArray`, can be empty | Which memory (loom) an agent wakes up with, in place of the one the interaction chooses: a JSON array of `{ "agentName": "wren", "name": "people" }`, naming each loom by `name` (or `name@namespace`) or by `id`. The interaction must have memory turned on. Pass `"[]"` for none. |
| `aiModelOverrides` | `jsonArray`, can be empty | Models to run some of the agents on, for this run only: a JSON array of `{ "agentName": "writer", "modelName": "deepseek.deepseek-v4-flash" }`, or with `customModel` in place of `modelName` for a model defined inline. These replace, rather than add to, the overrides this app run was started with. Pass `"[]"` for none. |
| `responseJsonSchema` | `string`, can be empty | A JSON Schema, as text, that the run's answer must match in place of the interaction's own. Pass `""` to use the interaction's. |

**Returns** `string`: The new run's id.

Name the interaction as `name`, or `name@namespace` for one in another namespace of your tenant; a name without `@` is looked up in this app's namespace. The run uses the interaction's latest enabled version.

Pass every argument, even the ones you don't use: `InteractionStart("brainstorm", inputs, "[]", "[]", "")`.

Start several runs before you wait, and they run at the same time: wait for them with [`InteractionAwait`](#interactionawait), [`InteractionAwaitAll`](#interactionawaitall) or [`InteractionAwaitAny`](#interactionawaitany).

The run is a child of this app run: its `parentProcessId` is this run, and it shares this run's `rootProcessId`. It uses this run's model keys (and its credential stack, when this run's start chose one), this run's model overrides when you give none, and the time limits and web settings this run was started with.

Fails when the interaction or its namespace doesn't exist (`Interaction 'brainstorm' was not found in namespace 'demo'.`), when an input is missing, empty, the wrong type or unknown to the interaction (`… requires input for product - but value was empty`), when a JSON argument has the wrong shape, when the schema isn't a valid JSON Schema, or when your plan refuses the start.

### InteractionStartWithLoomGifts

Starts an interaction run, as [`InteractionStart`](#interactionstart) does, handing some of its agents threads of memory as they start; returns the run's id straight away.

```c
string InteractionStartWithLoomGifts(string name, jsonObject inputs, jsonArray loomMappings, jsonArray aiModelOverrides, string responseJsonSchema, jsonArray loomGifts)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The interaction to start: `name`, or `name@namespace`. |
| `inputs` | `jsonObject` | The run's inputs, as a JSON object with one key per input, such as `{ "product": "a bamboo cup" }`. Text values are passed as they are; any other JSON value is passed as JSON text. Build it with [`JsonObjectCreate`](json.md#jsonobjectcreate) and [`JsonObjectSetString`](json.md#jsonobjectsetstring). This argument can't be empty: pass `"{}"` when the interaction takes no inputs. |
| `loomMappings` | `jsonArray`, can be empty | Which memory (loom) an agent wakes up with, in place of the one the interaction chooses: a JSON array of `{ "agentName": "wren", "name": "people" }`, naming each loom by `name` (or `name@namespace`) or by `id`. The interaction must have memory turned on. Pass `"[]"` for none. |
| `aiModelOverrides` | `jsonArray`, can be empty | Models to run some of the agents on, for this run only: a JSON array of `{ "agentName": "writer", "modelName": "deepseek.deepseek-v4-flash" }`, or with `customModel` in place of `modelName` for a model defined inline. These replace, rather than add to, the overrides this app run was started with. Pass `"[]"` for none. |
| `responseJsonSchema` | `string`, can be empty | A JSON Schema, as text, that the run's answer must match in place of the interaction's own. Pass `""` to use the interaction's. |
| `loomGifts` | `jsonArray` | The threads to hand over: a JSON array of `{ "agentName": "helper", "fromLoomId": "…", "threadIds": ["…"], "note": "…", "givenBy": "Wren" }`. Each gift holds 1 to 20 thread ids from one of your tenant's looms. `note`, a sentence the agent reads with them, and `givenBy`, who the agent is told gave them (at most 60 characters), are optional. Pass `"[]"` for none. |

**Returns** `string`: The new run's id.

An agent given threads wakes up knowing them, and knowing who told it. Only shared knowledge is handed over, never knots, private notes, reflections or episodes; the agent must have a loom in the interaction; and a start hands over at most 50 threads in all.

Everything else works as in [`InteractionStart`](#interactionstart), and fails in the same ways; a gift is refused when its loom or a thread isn't found, or the agent already wakes up with that loom.

### InteractionStartWithSwarmLimits

Starts an interaction run, as [`InteractionStartWithLoomGifts`](#interactionstartwithloomgifts) does, narrowing how far its sub-interactions may spread; returns the run's id straight away.

```c
string InteractionStartWithSwarmLimits(string name, jsonObject inputs, jsonArray loomMappings, jsonArray aiModelOverrides, string responseJsonSchema, jsonArray loomGifts, jsonObject swarmLimits)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The interaction to start: `name`, or `name@namespace`. |
| `inputs` | `jsonObject` | The run's inputs, as a JSON object with one key per input, such as `{ "product": "a bamboo cup" }`. Text values are passed as they are; any other JSON value is passed as JSON text. Build it with [`JsonObjectCreate`](json.md#jsonobjectcreate) and [`JsonObjectSetString`](json.md#jsonobjectsetstring). This argument can't be empty: pass `"{}"` when the interaction takes no inputs. |
| `loomMappings` | `jsonArray`, can be empty | Which memory (loom) an agent wakes up with, in place of the one the interaction chooses: a JSON array of `{ "agentName": "wren", "name": "people" }`, naming each loom by `name` (or `name@namespace`) or by `id`. The interaction must have memory turned on. Pass `"[]"` for none. |
| `aiModelOverrides` | `jsonArray`, can be empty | Models to run some of the agents on, for this run only: a JSON array of `{ "agentName": "writer", "modelName": "deepseek.deepseek-v4-flash" }`, or with `customModel` in place of `modelName` for a model defined inline. These replace, rather than add to, the overrides this app run was started with. Pass `"[]"` for none. |
| `responseJsonSchema` | `string`, can be empty | A JSON Schema, as text, that the run's answer must match in place of the interaction's own. Pass `""` to use the interaction's. |
| `loomGifts` | `jsonArray`, can be empty | Threads to hand to the agents as they start, as [`InteractionStartWithLoomGifts`](#interactionstartwithloomgifts) takes them. Pass `"[]"` for none. |
| `swarmLimits` | `jsonObject` | The limits, as a JSON object: `maxDepth` (levels of sub-interactions below this run, 0 to 4), `maxConcurrent` (runs going at once, 0 to 20) and `maxTotal` (runs started over the tree's life, 0 to 100), each optional. This argument can't be empty: pass `"{}"` to narrow nothing. |

**Returns** `string`: The new run's id.

Each limit you give becomes the lower of it and the interaction's own, and a limit you leave out isn't narrowed: nothing here can raise a limit. A limit out of its range is refused.

Everything else works as in [`InteractionStart`](#interactionstart), and fails in the same ways.

### InteractionVoteNo

Votes no, as a person, on the vote or proposed solution an interaction run is waiting on, giving a reason.

```c
void InteractionVoteNo(string processId, string reason, string authorName, string authorId)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `string` | The interaction run's id. |
| `reason` | `string` | Why: what the agents should change. It can't be blank. |
| `authorName` | `string`, can be empty | The name the vote is shown as coming from. There is no default: `""` records no name. |
| `authorId` | `string`, can be empty | The id of the user to record as the voter. Pass `""` for the user this app runs as. |

The agents read the reason. The run must be waiting for a person (`HumanInteractionRequired`) on a vote or a proposed solution; it carries on once the vote is in. A run that ended because nobody voted in time is woken up again.

Fails with `Reason is required` for a blank reason, and otherwise as [`InteractionVoteYes`](#interactionvoteyes) does.

### InteractionVoteYes

Votes yes, as a person, on the vote or proposed solution an interaction run is waiting on.

```c
void InteractionVoteYes(string processId, string authorName, string authorId)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `string` | The interaction run's id. |
| `authorName` | `string`, can be empty | The name the vote is shown as coming from. There is no default: `""` records no name. |
| `authorId` | `string`, can be empty | The id of the user to record as the voter. Pass `""` for the user this app runs as. |

The run must be waiting for a person (`HumanInteractionRequired`) on a vote or a proposed solution; it carries on once the vote is in. A run that ended because nobody voted in time is woken up again.

Fails with `Interaction process is not ready for human input` when the run isn't waiting for a person (it is working, or has ended), `Interaction process is not waiting for a vote` or `Interaction process is in neither vote or solution proposal mode` when there is nothing to vote on, and `Not found` when your tenant has no interaction run with that id.
